provider: Derived basic statistical references from World Tourism Organization (UNWTO), Yearbook of Tourism Statistics2023, data2017–2021
methodology: Newly calculated leading-country reference lists from2019 factual observations. Source prose, layout, regional aggregates and complete source tables are not reproduced. Original yearbook tables have different populations; their definitions are retained. Full coordinate extract stays work-only. Outbound references use ONLY one-year table1 border tourist arrivals by residence and are explicitly partial destination-reported samples.

inbound.label: Arrivals of non-resident visitors at national borders, by nationality
inbound.scope: 2019 border visitor arrivals, classified by nationality. These are source-country categories in the selected published table, not a measured ranking of unique people.
inbound.note: A historical baseline derived from basic published statistics. The atlas retains the leading20 positions, including boundary ties; missing cells, grouped regions and domestic categories are excluded. Tables have different populations: border visitors, border tourists and accommodation arrivals are labelled per country and must not be compared as identical measures. It is not November–December2026 demand.
inbound.referenceNotice: 2019 baseline from UN Tourism’s2023 yearbook. This is a dated statistical reference, not a current forecast. Read whether the source counts nationality, residence, border visits or accommodation arrivals.

outbound.label: Destination-reported border tourist arrivals by usual residence
outbound.scope: Partial reporting sample: 62 destination countries/territories with2019 border-tourist arrival tables classified by usual residence. Each row is reported by the destination, not a departure count from the selected country.
outbound.note: Derived by transposing only table1 residence-based border tourist observations in one year. This is the leading observed destinations within that sample, not an exhaustive worldwide outbound ranking or a resident departure survey. Important destinations absent from this sample can be missing from the list. Repeated visits count separately; missing values are not zero. Nationality-based, same-day-visitor and accommodation tables are excluded. Current national tables take priority when available.
outbound.referenceNotice: 2019 partial destination-reported sample (62 reporters). This reference cannot establish a complete global top20 or current resident travel demand. Each row links to its reporting destination’s source page.
